beats.headline: NESSIE CAUGHT?
beats.short_title: The Famous Loch Ness Photo Was FAKE 🦕 Case #22 Meatball Investigates
beats.comment: Do you still believe in Nessie? 🦕 yes / 🙅 no
beats.bonus: The 1934 'Surgeon's Photograph' made the Loch Ness Monster famous. In 1994 it was revealed as a hoax: the 'neck' was a sculpted head on a toy submarine. A 2018 environmental-DNA survey of the loch led by Prof. Neil Gemmell found no reptile DNA, but a lot of eel DNA.
beats.caption: The most famous Nessie photo was a toy submarine.
sources: Wikipedia, Loch Ness Monster: 'Surgeon's Photograph' (1934) shown in 1994 to be a hoax using a toy submarine fitted with a sculpted head (Christian Spurling); 2018 eDNA survey (Neil Gemmell, University of Otago) found no reptile DNA and a lot of eel DNA — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loch_Ness_Monster (checked 2026-10-26)
Gemmell et al., Loch Ness eDNA survey results, University of Otago, September 2019

beats.headline: BALLOON TANKS?
beats.short_title: The Ghost Army Fooled Germany With Balloon Tanks 🎈 Case #24
beats.comment: Would you have been fooled? 🎈 yes / 🧐 no
beats.bonus: The Ghost Army (23rd Headquarters Special Troops) was a 1,100-man US unit in WWII that used inflatable tanks, sound trucks playing recorded tank noise and fake radio traffic to mislead German forces in more than 20 operations. Many of its soldiers were artists, including Bill Blass and Ellsworth Kelly. It stayed secret until 1996 and received the Congressional Gold Medal in 2022.
beats.caption: A secret US Army unit fought WWII with balloon tanks and fake sounds.

Bill Blass and Ellsworth Kelly; declassified 1996; Congressional Gold Medal February 2022 — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_Army (checked 2026-10-26)
Rick Beyer and Elizabeth Sayles, 'The Ghost Army of World War II' (Princeton Architectural Press, 2015)

beats.say: Air Force planes flew over the jungle, and made it rain.
beats.headline: WEATHER WARFARE?
beats.short_title: The US Really Used WEATHER as a Weapon 🌧️ Case #25
beats.comment: Should weather be a weapon? 🌧️ yes / 🙅 never
beats.bonus: Operation Popeye (1967-1972) was a secret US Air Force program that seeded clouds over the Ho Chi Minh Trail to lengthen the monsoon and turn supply roads to mud. Its crews' slogan was 'make mud, not war'. After it came out, the 1977 ENMOD convention banned hostile weather modification.
beats.caption: The US really seeded clouds to make war rain.
sources: Wikipedia, Operation Popeye: highly classified US Air Force cloud-seeding program over the Ho Chi Minh Trail, 1967-1972, using silver iodide and lead iodide to extend the monsoon and turn roads to mud; flown by the 54th Weather Reconnaissance Squadron under the slogan 'make mud, not war'; exposed in the 1970s; followed by the 1977 ENMOD convention banning hostile environmental modification — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Popeye (checked 2026-10-26)

beats.headline: THE MISSING LINK?
beats.short_title: Piltdown Man: The Fossil That Fooled Science for 41 Years 💀 Case #26
beats.comment: Would you have been fooled? 💀 yes / 🧐 no
beats.bonus: Piltdown Man, 'found' in 1912 by amateur archaeologist Charles Dawson, was hailed as a missing link between apes and humans. In 1953 it was exposed as a forgery: a modern human skull combined with an orangutan's jaw and filed-down teeth. It fooled experts for 41 years, and a 2016 study concluded Dawson made it.
beats.caption: The 'missing link' was a fake, and it fooled science for 41 years.
sources: Wikipedia, Piltdown Man: announced 1912 (Charles Dawson); exposed as a forgery in 1953; modern human cranium plus an orangutan mandible with filed-down teeth; 41 years; 2016 review concluded Dawson was the hoaxer — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piltdown_Man (checked 2026-10-26)
De Groote et al., 'New genetic and morphological evidence suggests a single hoaxer created Piltdown man', Royal Society Open Science, 2016

beats.say: Pigeons were trained to steer a bomb, by pecking a screen.
beats.headline: PIGEON PILOTS?
beats.short_title: The US Trained Pigeons to Steer Missiles 🐦 Case #27 Meatball Investigates
beats.comment: Would you trust a pigeon pilot? 🐦 yes / 🙅 no
beats.bonus: Project Pigeon: in WWII psychologist B. F. Skinner trained pigeons to guide a bomb by pecking at the target's image on a screen in the nose. It was cancelled in 1944, revived by the Navy in 1948 as Project Orcon, and cancelled for good in 1953 when electronic guidance worked.
beats.caption: B. F. Skinner really trained pigeons to steer bombs.
sources: Wikipedia, Project Pigeon: B. F. Skinner's WWII pigeon-guided bomb; lenses projected the target onto a screen and trained pigeons pecked at it to steer; one bird pecked more than 10,000 times in 45 minutes; cancelled 8 October 1944; revived by the Navy in 1948 as Project Orcon and cancelled in 1953 when electronic guidance proved reliable — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Pigeon (checked 2026-10-26)
B. F. Skinner, 'Pigeons in a Pelican', American Psychologist 15 (1960)
